artworks.context: The sitter is Lisa Gherardini, wife of the Florentine merchant Francesco del Giocondo. Leonardo kept the portrait and continued working on it. Soft transitions of tone connect her face with a distant landscape.

artworks.title: The Scream
artworks.medium: Tempera and grease crayon on cardboard
artworks.context: This is the National Museum’s 1893 painted version. Its landscape is the Oslo fjord seen from Ekeberg. The simplified figure and intense, curving colours connect the scene with Munch’s account of anxiety in nature.
artworks.imageCredit: Edvard Munch / National Museum of Norway; museum photography credited to Børre Høstland, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.
artworks.dimensionNote: Museum record explicitly gives width 73.5 × height 91 cm. Medium follows the current museum record, rather than the differing descriptions in some Commons filenames.
artworks.imageNote: Full artwork is preserved; the source image includes a narrow dark frame.

artworks.title: The Last Supper
artworks.context: Leonardo painted on dry plaster so that he could work slowly and revise the scene. Christ sits at the centre as the twelve apostles respond with varied gestures and emotions to his words.
artworks.imageCredit: Leonardo da Vinci / Santa Maria delle Grazie, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.
artworks.dimensionNote: Museum dimensions are height 460 × width 880 cm. Use this museum figure; the current Commons metadata for this image incorrectly gives a 700 cm height.
